verses.1: I have told you this detailed account of Nṛga's curse; if you have a desire to listen, then hear another story here.
verses.2: But thus spoken to by Rama, Saumitri spoke again, saying, "O king, I have no satisfaction from wonderful stories."
verses.3: But thus spoken to by Lakshmana, Rama, the delight of the Ikshvakus, began to narrate a most righteous story.
verses.4: There was a king named Nimi, the twelfth son among the noble Ikshvakus, who was firmly established in both valor and righteousness.
verses.5: That valiant king then founded a city, resembling a divine city, near the hermitage of Gautama.
verses.6: The city was known as Sukrita, or Vaijayanta, where the greatly renowned royal sage Nimi established his settlement.
verses.7: After establishing that magnificent city, the thought arose in him, "I should perform a long sacrifice, delighting my father's mind."
verses.8: Thereafter, having consulted his father Ikshvaku, the son of Manu, he first chose Vasishtha, the foremost among Brahmarishis, to officiate the sacrifice.
verses.9: Subsequently, the royal sage Nimi, a descendant of Ikshvaku, approached Atri, Angiras, and Bhrigu, who were rich in penance.
verses.10: However, Vasishtha said to Nimi, the best of royal sages, "I have already been chosen by Indra, so please wait for some time."
verses.11: Subsequently, the great brahmin Gautama fulfilled Nimi's request, while the greatly effulgent Vasishtha then performed Indra's sacrifice.
verses.12: King Nimi, the lord of men, however, gathered those brahmins and performed a sacrifice near his own city, on the side of the Himalayas, undertaking the sacrificial vow for five thousand years.
verses.13: However, at the conclusion of Indra's sacrifice, the blameless divine sage Vasishtha came near the king to perform the role of the hotri priest.
verses.14: Then, Vasiṣṭha, the son of Brahma, saw the place occupied by Gautama and was overcome with great anger.
verses.15: Desirous of seeing the king, Vasiṣṭha sat down for a moment, but on that day, the royal sage was deeply overcome by sleep.
verses.16: Then, anger arose in the great-souled Vasiṣṭha due to the absence of the royal sage, and he began to speak.
verses.17: "O King, because you have chosen another, disregarding me, your body will become devoid of consciousness."
verses.18: Then, the royal sage, awakened and having heard the uttered curse, spoke to Vasiṣṭha, the son of Brahma, overcome with fury and anger.
verses.19: Enraged by anger, he, unaware of me sleeping, cast upon me the fire of a curse, like a second rod of Yama.
verses.20: Therefore, O Brahmarshi, without a doubt, even your exceedingly charming body will be deprived of consciousness.
verses.21: Thus, under the sway of anger, both the king and the chief of Brahmins, having cursed each other, suddenly became bodiless, each possessing an equally acquired power. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 55 ।। Thus ends the fifty-fifth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
